symbols.name: s
symbols.def: Generic rank in the Perron-priority reveal order.

symbols.name: G_n
symbols.def: Known labeled interference relation on \(\mathcal I_n\); simplicity and undirectedness are imposed separately.

symbols.name: \mathcal H_n
symbols.def: Formal direct-effect conflict graph operator \(\mathcal H_n=I_n+A_{G_n}\), including one loop at each unit.

symbols.name: \pi_n
symbols.def: Unit-to-rank permutation: \(\pi_n(i)=1\) is the first reveal, and within each connected component of \(G_n\), smaller ranks correspond to larger positive unit-norm Perron coordinates of \(\mathcal H_n\), with label ties and components broken by the smallest label.

symbols.name: p_n
symbols.def: Probability \(p_n=(2\lambda_n)^{-1}\) that a desired-exposure coordinate is nonnull.

symbols.name: \mathbb P_U
symbols.def: Probability under the product law of \(U_{n,i}\), conditional on the fixed graph and potential outcomes.

symbols.name: Z_n
symbols.def: Assignment returned by Algorithm 1 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} with \(r=2\), formal direct-effect conflict graph \(\mathcal H_n\), rank map \(\pi_n\), and desired coordinates \(U_{n,i}\).

symbols.name: Y_{n,i}(\mathbf z)
symbols.def: Fixed potential outcome of unit \(i\) under assignment \(\mathbf z\).

symbols.name: \mathbf e_{n,i}
symbols.def: Assignment treating \(i\) and no other unit.

symbols.name: C_0
symbols.def: A universal finite positive constant large enough for the stated moment and ratio bounds.

symbols.name: C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)
symbols.def: Finite constant depending only on \(B\) and \(c\).

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: Fixed tolerance for variance-bound ratio concentration.

symbols.name: d_{\mathrm K}
symbols.def: Kolmogorov distance \(d_{\mathrm K}(X,Z)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}|\mathbb P(X\le x)-\mathbb P(Z\le x)|\).

symbols.name: \mathsf P_n
symbols.def: Matrix with \((\mathsf P_n)_{ji}=1\) exactly when \(j\in B_{n,i}\), so rows index earlier parents and columns index later children.

symbols.name: S_{n,i}
symbols.def: Independent Rademacher sign encoding labels \(1\) and \(0\) on the event \(R_{n,i}=1\).

symbols.name: \mathcal F_{n,s}
symbols.space: A filtration on the product assignment space.
symbols.def: Rank-indexed filtration \(\mathcal F_{n,0}=\{\varnothing,\Omega\}\) and \(\mathcal F_{n,s}=\sigma(U_{n,\rho_n(1)},\ldots,U_{n,\rho_n(s)})\) for \(1\le s\le n\).

symbols.name: M_{n,s}
symbols.def: Rank-\(s\) increment \(M_{n,s}=\mathbb E_U[F_n\mid\mathcal F_{n,s}]-\mathbb E_U[F_n\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1}]\).

symbols.name: \Delta_{n,s}Q_n
symbols.def: Signed coordinate difference of \(Q_n\) between setting \(R_{n,\rho_n(s)}=1\) and setting \(R_{n,\rho_n(s)}=0\), holding all other reveal coordinates fixed.

symbols.name: C_{\mathrm W}(B,c,\alpha)
symbols.def: Finite constant depending only on \(B\), \(c\), and \(\alpha\).

symbols.name: \mathcal R_n(d;B,c)
symbols.def: Exact order, up to constants, of \(K_n(d;B,c)\), to be derived by \(\mathrm{oeq:optimal\text{-}kolmogorov\text{-}rate}\).

assumptions.condition: \(G_n\) is a simple undirected graph on \(\mathcal I_n\).
\(Y_{n,i}(\mathbf z)=Y_{n,i}(\mathbf z')\) whenever \(z_j=z'_j\) for every \(j\in\{i\}\cup\mathcal N_{G_n}(i)\).

definitions.name: Perron priority order
definitions.construction: For each connected component of \(G_n\), take a positive unit-norm Perron eigenvector of the component block of \(\mathcal H_n\), assign ranks by decreasing coordinate with label ties, and concatenate components by their smallest label. This defines the unit-to-rank map \(\pi_n\), its inverse \(\rho_n=\pi_n^{-1}\), and \(B_{n,i}=\{j:\{i,j\}\in G_n,\ \pi_n(j)<\pi_n(i)\}\).

definitions.name: Independent desired-exposure law
definitions.construction: Independently for \(i\in\mathcal I_n\), draw \(U_{n,i}=1\) and \(U_{n,i}=0\) with probability \((4\lambda_n)^{-1}\) each and draw \(U_{n,i}=*\) with probability \(t_n=1-(2\lambda_n)^{-1}\); set \(E_{n,i,k}=\{U_{n,i}=k,\ U_{n,j}=*\text{ for all }j\in B_{n,i}\}\) and \(q_{n,i}=(4\lambda_n)^{-1}t_n^{|B_{n,i}|}\).

definitions.name: Fixed \(r=2\) Conflict Graph Design
definitions.construction: Apply Algorithm 1 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} with \(r=2\), formal direct-effect conflict graph \(\mathcal H_n\), rank map \(\pi_n\), and coordinates \(U_{n,i}\) to obtain \(Z_n\); the strict earlier-neighbor sets are \(B_{n,i}\) from \(G_n\). On \(E_{n,i,1}\) the algorithm realizes \(\mathbf e_{n,i}\) in unit \(i\)'s closed \(G_n\)-neighborhood, and on \(E_{n,i,0}\) it realizes \(\mathbf 0_n\) there.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\)
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)=\left\{(G_n,Y_n):\ G_n\text{ is simple and undirected},\ Y_n\text{ satisfies arbitrary neighborhood interference on }G_n,\ D_n\le d,\ \frac1n\sum_i|a_{n,i}|^4\le B,\ \frac1n\sum_i|b_{n,i}|^4\le B,\ \sigma_n^2\ge\frac{c\lambda_n}{n}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: Forward CGD Doob decomposition
definitions.construction: At reveal rank \(s\), let \(J_{n,s}=\sum_{i:(\mathsf P_n)_{\rho_n(s),i}=1}\delta_{n,i}h_{n,i,<s}\), \(C_{n,s}=\delta_{n,\rho_n(s)}h_{n,\rho_n(s)}/p_n-J_{n,s}/t_n\), and \(G_{n,s}=\gamma_{n,\rho_n(s)}h_{n,\rho_n(s)}/p_n\). The coordinate identity to audit is \[M_{n,s}=C_{n,s}(R_{n,\rho_n(s)}-p_n)+G_{n,s}R_{n,\rho_n(s)}S_{n,\rho_n(s)},\qquad Q_n=p_n\sum_{s=1}^n\{t_nC_{n,s}^2+G_{n,s}^2\}.\]

definitions.name: Critical repeated-star construction
definitions.construction: For fixed \(\beta>0\), take \(k_n=\lfloor\beta n^{2/3}\rfloor\), \(m_n=\lfloor n/(k_n+1)\rfloor\) disjoint stars with \(k_n\) leaves, and isolated padding vertices; put \(a_{n,i}=1,b_{n,i}=0\) on leaves and \(a_{n,i}=b_{n,i}=0\) elsewhere.

definitions.name: CGD Kolmogorov-rate handle
definitions.construction: Determine \(\mathcal R_n(d;B,c)\) by pairing the forward martingale moment terms from \(\mathrm{def:doob\text{-}decomposition}\) with lower bounds obtained from optimized legal block-star arrays and perturbations of their hub-trigger counts.

statements.statement: For every \((G_n,Y_n)\in\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\), \(1\le\lambda_n\le D_n\), \(\lambda_n\ge\sqrt{D_n}\), \(|B_{n,i}|\le\lambda_n-1\), and the oriented matrix satisfies \(\|\mathsf P_n\|_{2\to2}\le\lambda_n\), \(\|\mathsf P_n\|_{4\to4}\le\sqrt{\lambda_nD_n}\), and \(\|\mathsf P_n^{\top}\|_{4\to4}\le\lambda_n\).
statements.justification: These inequalities translate Perron priority into the operator norms needed to avoid a squared dependency neighborhood.
statements.gap: \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} uses Perron order for design and variance control but not this \(\ell_4\) martingale chain.
statements.consumer: The prefix and operator bounds are the deterministic input to the uniform normal-approximation theorem.

statements.statement: For the rank-indexed filtration in \(\mathrm{def:doob\text{-}decomposition}\), the displayed coordinate formula satisfies \(F_n-\mathbb E_UF_n=\sum_{s=1}^nM_{n,s}\), \(\mathbb E_U[M_{n,s}\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1}]=0\), and \(Q_n=\sum_{s=1}^n\mathbb E_U[M_{n,s}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1}]\), with \(\mathbb E_UQ_n=n^2\sigma_n^2\).
statements.justification: This proposed identity exposes the independent-coordinate filtration that the published unit-level dependency graph discards.
statements.gap: Algorithm 1 in \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} is sequential, but its published CLT does not derive these increments.
statements.consumer: An independently verified identity would permit direct use of quantitative martingale normal approximation.

statements.statement: The candidate universal constant \(C_0<\infty\) can be chosen so that uniformly over \(\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\), \[\sum_{s=1}^n\mathbb E_U|M_{n,s}|^4\le C_0Bn\lambda_nD_n^2,\qquad \operatorname{Var}_U(Q_n)\le C_0Bn\lambda_n^2D_n.\] At every reveal rank \(s\), the Bernoulli coordinate flip is conjectured to obey \[|\Delta_{n,s}Q_n|\le64p_n[\mathsf P_n\operatorname{diag}(w_n)(\lambda_nv_n+\mathsf P_n^{\top}v_n)]_{\rho_n(s)}.\]
statements.justification: This is the answer-open early-kill lemma: D0 must prove or refute it for overlapping prefixes and arbitrary signed endpoints.
statements.gap: Neither \cite{Haeusler1988MartingaleRate} nor \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} supplies a CGD-specific graph-uniform predictable-variation bound.
statements.consumer: If established, it would supply the candidate \(n^{2/3}\) normal regime without imposing a maximum-outcome bound.

statements.statement: For each fixed \(B\ge1\) and \(0<c\le1\), the constant \(C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)<\infty\) may be chosen so that every member of \(\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\) satisfies \[d_{\mathrm K}((T_n-\tau_n)/\sigma_n,Z_0)\le\min\left\{1,C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)\left(\frac{D_n^2}{n\lambda_n}+\frac{D_n}{n}\right)^{1/5}\right\}\le\min\left\{1,C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)\left(\frac{D_n^{3/2}}n\right)^{1/5}\right\}.\] Consequently \(K_n(d;B,c)\le\min\{1,C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)(d^{3/2}/n)^{1/5}\}\).
statements.justification: This is a candidate quantitative consequence of the independently unverified rank-indexed martingale and prefix-flip bounds.
statements.gap: Theorem 5.6 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} requires \(d=o(n^{1/9})\); direct substitution of Theorem 2.3 of \cite{JanischLehericy2024SparseDependencyGraph} at \(\delta=4\) uses a generic dependency graph and does not attain this bound.
statements.consumer: If proved, future CGD replications could check the graph-degree growth rule before replacing conservative Chebyshev calibration by a normal critical value.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\beta>0\), the construction in \(\mathrm{def:repeated\text{-}star\text{-}witness}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_n(k_n+1;B,c)\) eventually for every fixed \(B\ge1\) and \(0<c\le1\), has \(D_n/n^{2/3}\to\beta\), and satisfies \[(T_n-\tau_n)/\sigma_n\Rightarrow\mathcal L_{\beta}=\mathcal L\left(\sqrt{8/9}Z_0-\frac{N_{r_{\beta}}-r_{\beta}}{3\sqrt{r_{\beta}}}\right).\] The law \(\mathcal L_{\beta}\) has variance one and nonzero third cumulant \(-1/(27\sqrt{r_{\beta}})\), so it is not \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).
statements.justification: This conjectural critical compound limit is the proposed legal obstruction under the original fourth moments and variance floor.
statements.gap: Proposition 5.8 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} alternates a single star with another graph and does not locate the worst-case degree boundary.
statements.consumer: If independently proved, the construction would supply necessity for degree envelopes that are not \(o(n^{2/3})\).

statements.statement: For every fixed \(B\ge1\), every fixed \(0<c\le1\), and every integer sequence \(1\le d_n\le n\), \[K_n(d_n;B,c)\longrightarrow0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d_n=o(n^{2/3}).\] No additional slowly varying boundary factor is present.
statements.justification: This candidate iff statement is the field-tier target, contingent on D0 verification of both the martingale upper bound and the repeated-star limit.
statements.gap: No cited paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient degree condition for the fixed \(r=2\) CGD estimator; \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} gives only \(1/9\) sufficiency and a nonsharp obstruction.
statements.consumer: A verified frontier would supply a single asymptotic design rule for deciding when CGD normal inference is uniformly justified.

statements.statement: The universal constant \(C_0<\infty\) may be chosen so that every \((G_n,Y_n)\in\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\) satisfies \[L_n\le C_0\lambda_n,\qquad n^2\sigma_n^2\le L_nH_{2,n},\qquad \mathbb E_U\widehat H_{2,n}=H_{2,n},\qquad \operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat H_{2,n})\le2C_0Bn\lambda_n.\]
statements.justification: This proposed squared-endpoint reduction would turn the published CGD operator inequality into uniform moment control for the observable scale.
statements.gap: Propositions 5.3--5.4 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} establish additive and ratio consistency for the spectral variance-bound estimator, respectively, but not this fixed-class quantitative package.
statements.consumer: The inequalities supply the denominator and numerator controls for uniform ratio consistency.

statements.statement: The universal constant \(C_0<\infty\) may be chosen so that every \((G_n,Y_n)\in\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\) obeys \(\mathrm{VB}_n\ge\sigma_n^2>0\) and, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\mathbb P_U\left(\left|\frac{\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n}{\mathrm{VB}_n}-1\right|>\varepsilon\right)\le\frac{C_0B\lambda_n}{c^2n\varepsilon^2}.\] Consequently the class supremum is at most \(C_0Bd/(c^2n\varepsilon^2)\), so the ratio converges to one uniformly whenever \(d_n=o(n)\), including the sharp normal regime.
statements.justification: This expanded-regime ratio statement is a candidate downstream consequence and is not treated as established before D0 verification.
statements.gap: Propositions 5.3--5.4 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} establish additive and ratio consistency, respectively, while \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance} explains why exact variance cannot replace this bound.
statements.consumer: If proved, it would make the candidate normal frontier usable with observed outcomes rather than the inaccessible exact variance.

statements.statement: For each fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the constant \(C_{\mathrm W}(B,c,\alpha)<\infty\) may be chosen so that \[\inf_{(G_n,Y_n)\in\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)}\mathbb P_U(\tau_n\in C_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha-2K_n(d;B,c)-C_{\mathrm W}(B,c,\alpha)(d/n)^{1/3}.\] Hence, if \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\), then \(\liminf_n\inf_{\mathcal M_n(d_n;B,c)}\mathbb P_U(\tau_n\in C_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: This expanded-regime coverage statement is a candidate downstream consequence of the unverified normal and ratio bounds.
statements.gap: Corollary 5.7 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} covers only its \(o(n^{1/9})\) pointwise regime.
statements.consumer: If proved, it would provide the CGD calibration rule for the concrete direct-effect inquiry in Declaration 18.13.

statements.statement: If \(G_n\) is edgeless, then \(D_n=\lambda_n=1\), every \(B_{n,i}=\varnothing\), and \(q_{n,i}=1/4\). The fixed \(r=2\) CGD estimator is therefore a sum of independent modified Horvitz--Thompson endpoint contrasts, and \(K_n(1;B,c)\to0\), recovering the classical independent triangular-array central limit theorem under the stated fourth moments and variance floor.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check at the no-interference boundary.
statements.gap: This is a consistency check against classical Berry--Esseen theory rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It verifies that the frontier does not distort ordinary independent randomization inference.

statements.statement: Conditional on D0 validating the candidate frontier, what is the exact order \(\mathcal R_n(d;B,c)\), up to constants depending only on \(B\) and \(c\), of \(K_n(d;B,c)\) throughout the resulting Gaussian regime; in particular, can legal CGD graph-and-endpoint arrays match each dominant verified martingale error term?
statements.justification: This secondary question is conditional: the degree frontier and its internal rate bound must first survive the answer-open D0 audit.
statements.gap: Exactness in \cite{Haeusler1988MartingaleRate} ranges over general martingales, and optimality in \cite{JanischLehericy2024SparseDependencyGraph} ranges over general dependency graphs; neither proves attainability by CGD arrays.
statements.consumer: A matched rate would quantify how conservative the asymptotic degree rule is at the finite graph sizes used in experiment planning.

sampling_model.design: Known fixed \(r=2\) Conflict Graph Design using the formal direct-effect conflict graph \(\mathcal H_n=I_n+A_{G_n}\), generated from independent desired-exposure coordinates in Perron-priority rank order.
sampling_model.units: One triangular array of \(n\) fixed labeled units with fixed graph and fixed potential outcomes; there is no super-population sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: The only randomness is \(U_{n,i}\), and Algorithm 1 maps it to the realized binary assignment \(Z_n\).
sampling_model.overlap: The endpoint exposure probability is known exactly as \(q_{n,i}=(4\lambda_n)^{-1}t_n^{|B_{n,i}|}\); for edgeless \(G_n\), \(\lambda_n=1\), \(B_{n,i}=\varnothing\), and \(q_{n,i}=1/4\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no statistical nuisance functions; \(\lambda_n\), \(q_{n,i}\), and \(\mathbf V_n\) are design-computable.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.6 proves asymptotic normality when the maximum conflict degree is \(o(n^{1/9})\).
Proposition 5.8 constructs a direct-effect sequence whose standardized CGD estimator does not converge in distribution.
Propositions 5.3 and 5.4 establish additive and ratio consistency, respectively, for the spectral variance-bound estimator.
Corollary 5.7 gives conservative Wald coverage under the paper's sufficient CLT regime.

Theorem 2.3 gives a Kolmogorov bound for dependency-graph sums with finite \(L^{\delta}\) moments for \(\delta\in[3,\infty)\); the direct fourth-moment substitution here sets \(\delta=4\). Theorem 2.1 is the bounded-summand result, and Theorem 2.4 treats \(\delta\in(2,3)\), so neither is the direct comparison for this class.
The discrete-time theorem bounds martingale normal approximation using increment moments and normalized predictable quadratic variation.
The paper characterizes admissible estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and complex designs.
The preprint derives design-based upper and lower bounds on minimax mean-squared point-estimation risk in terms of local and global conflict-graph connectivity.

tldr: For the fixed \(r=2\) Conflict Graph Design estimator, the candidate field-tier answer is a sharp uniform normal-inference frontier at \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\), with a quantitative prefix-sensitive martingale bound, a repeated-star Gaussian--Poisson obstruction at the boundary, uniform ratio consistency for the published spectral variance-bound estimator, and conservative feasible Wald coverage. Every new bound, boundary law, frontier, and expanded-regime inference claim remains a to-prove presolve target: D0 must independently validate the rank-indexed Doob identity, the coordinate-flip/operator chain, and the repeated-star limit before the exponent or absence of a slowly varying factor is accepted.

project_justification.gap: The published CGD theorem proves normality only under \(d_{\max}=o(n^{1/9})\), while its counterexample lies in a much denser regime; later generic dependency bounds do not resolve the intervening CGD-specific range.
project_justification.niche: Algorithm 1 is generated from ordered independent desired-exposure coordinates, which suggests a rank-indexed martingale structure hidden by reduction to two-hop dependency neighborhoods.
project_justification.fill: The project tests the candidate prefix-sensitive martingale bound against legal critical repeated-star failures and, only if both survive D0, carries the resulting iff frontier through the observable spectral variance bound to conservative Wald coverage.

related_work: \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} supplies the fixed \(r=2\) design, estimator, spectral variance bound, \(o(n^{1/9})\) sufficient CLT in Theorem 5.6, direct-effect nonconvergence construction in Proposition 5.8, additive consistency in Proposition 5.3, ratio consistency in Proposition 5.4, and Wald result in Corollary 5.7. Its formal direct-effect conflict graph has operator \(\mathcal H_n=I_n+A_{G_n}\); Appendix D.9 writes the star value as \(\sqrt{n-1}\) by suppressing the formal loop contribution, whereas the exact loop-inclusive value is \(1+\sqrt{n-1}\). The candidate statements would strictly strengthen the published distributional and coverage results if D0 verifies them. \cite{HeydeBrown1970DepartureNormality} and \cite{Haeusler1988MartingaleRate} supply the martingale normal-approximation template, while \cite{Bolthausen1982ExactMartingaleRates} and \cite{Mourrat2013MartingaleRate} clarify why conditional-variance fluctuations can govern exact behavior. Theorem 2.3 of \cite{JanischLehericy2024SparseDependencyGraph}, specialized to \(\delta=4\), is the direct finite-fourth-moment dependency-graph substitution; Theorem 2.1 applies only to bounded summands, and Theorem 2.4 addresses \(\delta\in(2,3)\). These results, together with \cite{Ross2011FundamentalsStein}, \cite{Chin2019SteinInterference}, and \cite{CaiShaoZhang2026RefinedLocalDependence}, inform the comparison but are not claimed to be sharpened as general probability theorems. \cite{KandirosHarshawSavje2026MinimaxNetwork} optimizes assignment designs and estimators for minimax mean-squared point-estimation risk under arbitrary neighborhood interference; it does not study the fixed \(r=2\) CGD estimator's Kolmogorov frontier or Wald coverage. \cite{AronowSamii2017GeneralInterference} provides the exposure-weighted design-based inference baseline. \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance} explains why inference targets an estimable conservative quadratic bound rather than the generally unidentified exact variance. Declaration 18.13 of \cite{BlairCoppockHumphreys2023ResearchDesign}, modeled after \cite{GreenKrasnoCoppockFarrerLenoirZingher2016LawnSigns}, supplies a concrete direct-effect consumer: its \(238\)-precinct queen-adjacency design defines \(\operatorname{mean}(Y_{1,0}-Y_{0,0})\), exactly the endpoint contrast considered here.
technical_internal_limitation: The \(n^{2/3}\) exponent is not an established result. Presolve algebra and finite graph-family enumeration motivate, but do not prove, the rank-indexed identity or \(\mathrm{lem:prefix\text{-}flip\text{-}moments}\). D0 must independently derive the formula with \(\pi_n\) unit-to-rank, \(\rho_n=\pi_n^{-1}\), and \(\mathcal F_{n,s}=\sigma(U_{n,\rho_n(1)},\ldots,U_{n,\rho_n(s)})\), then prove or refute the shared-child orientation \(\mathsf P_n\operatorname{diag}(w_n)\mathsf P_n^{\top}\), the square-difference constants, the Bernoulli tensorization factor, and the imported martingale inequality. It must also verify the repeated-star Gaussian--Poisson law. Failure under arbitrary signed endpoints withdraws the candidate frontier and all expanded-regime ratio and coverage consequences without adding assumptions.
honest_scope: The fixed \(r=2\) design, estimator algebra, endpoint class, and published spectral variance-bound target are settled inputs. Every new formal statement is marked \(\text{to-prove}\). In particular, \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\), the absence of a slowly varying boundary factor, the repeated-star law, the prefix-flip envelope, uniform ratio consistency beyond the published regime, and expanded-regime Wald coverage are conjectural presolve targets pending independent D0 verification. The target is a worst-case maximum-degree iff frontier, not a necessary condition for each graph sequence. The interval remains conservative because \(\mathrm{VB}_n\) can exceed \(\sigma_n^2\), and no exact-coverage or exact-variance-estimation claim is made. The theorem would be an asymptotic benchmark for future CGD replications and would not retroactively validate the Bernoulli assignment or Aronow--Samii intervals in Declaration 18.13.

Shortest uniformly honest CGD intervals beyond the Gaussian frontier.
Self-normalized CGD Berry--Esseen frontier using observable quadratic variation.

Exact uniform Kolmogorov convergence rate inside the Gaussian degree regime.

literature_map: The anchor is \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD}: Theorem 5.6 proves a dependency-graph CLT under \(d_{\max}=o(n^{1/9})\), Proposition 5.8 gives the direct-effect nonconvergence construction, Propositions 5.3--5.4 establish additive and ratio consistency for the spectral variance-bound estimator, and Corollary 5.7 gives Wald coverage in the published regime. The formal direct-effect conflict graph is \(\mathcal H_n\) with adjacency \(I_n+A_{G_n}\) and \(\lambda_n=1+\lambda_{\max}(A_{G_n})\); Appendix D.9's star display \(\sqrt{n-1}\) suppresses this formal \(+1\), so the exact loop-inclusive value is \(1+\sqrt{n-1}\). HeydeBrown1970DepartureNormality and Haeusler1988MartingaleRate convert fourth moments of Doob increments and predictable-quadratic-variation error into Kolmogorov control; Mourrat2013MartingaleRate explains why conditional-variance fluctuation can be an exact-rate obstruction. JanischLehericy2024SparseDependencyGraph gives its bounded-summand bound in Theorem 2.1, its finite-\(L^{\delta}\) bound for \(\delta\in[3,\infty)\) in Theorem 2.3, and its \(\delta\in(2,3)\) bound in Theorem 2.4; the direct substitution for this fourth-moment class is Theorem 2.3 at \(\delta=4\). CaiShaoZhang2026RefinedLocalDependence is a second generic local-dependence comparison. KandirosHarshawSavje2026MinimaxNetwork optimizes designs and estimators for minimax mean-squared point-estimation risk, a different problem from this fixed-design normal-approximation and Wald-coverage frontier. HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance characterizes conservative estimable quadratic bounds when exact randomization variance is unavailable; it informs but does not establish the candidate uniform CGD ratio theorem. AronowSamii2017GeneralInterference and Chin2019SteinInterference provide exposure and dependency-graph baselines. The opened sources do not establish the candidate CGD-specific rank martingale bound, necessary-and-sufficient degree frontier, repeated-star boundary law, or expanded-regime spectral-bound studentization.

novelty_justification.published_axis: If independently verified, the candidate core would advance the published sufficient condition \(d_{\max}=o(n^{1/9})\) to an iff frontier \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\), supply a quantitative rank-indexed prefix-martingale bound, and match it with legal repeated-star Gaussian--Poisson failures. The proposed uniform ratio and coverage statements are conditional downstream advances, not established presolve facts.
novelty_justification.repo_axis: The closest prior proposal supplied only a generic sufficient dependency-degree CLT, while the accepted SNIPE proposal concerns point-estimation risk and excludes variance estimation and limit laws. This proposal instead targets the fixed-design distributional frontier and feasible coverage for the published CGD estimator.

When normal confidence intervals work under Conflict Graph Design: a sharp degree frontier. For each n>=1 observe one design realization on n fixed labeled units with known simple undirected graph G and arbitrary-neighborhood-interference potential outcomes. Endpoint arrays a_i=Y_i(e_i), b_i=Y_i(0) define direct effect tau=n^-1 sum_i(a_i-b_i). H has adjacency I+A_G, lambda=lambda_max(H)>=1, D=max_i(1+deg_G(i)). Order each connected component by descending positive unit-norm Perron coordinate, ties by label; concatenate components by smallest label. B_i is the set of earlier neighbors. Independently sample U_i=1,0,* with probabilities 1/(4lambda),1/(4lambda),1-1/(2lambda). Fix r=2 and use published CGD Algorithm1 to realize E_ik={U_i=k, all earlier neighbors null}. Record U and observed outcomes. q_i=Pr(E_ik)=(4lambda)^-1(1-1/(2lambda))^|B_i|. T=n^-1 sum_i Yobs_i(1[E_i1]-1[E_i0])/q_i. For fixed B>=1 and 0<c<=1 impose n^-1 sum_i |a_i|^4<=B, n^-1 sum_i |b_i|^4<=B, and sigma²=Var_U(T)>=c lambda/n. Other potential outcomes unrestricted. No maximum-outcome bound or assumed CLT. All randomness is U. Define K_n(d;B,c)=sup over the specified fixed-design class with D<=d of sup_z |Pr_U((T-tau)/sigma<=z)-Phi(z)|, for integers 1<=d<=n. For each fixed B>=1,0<c<=1 determine an explicit necessary and sufficient growth condition on every integer sequence d_n for K_n(d_n;B,c)->0, including any essential slowly varying boundary factors. Derive a quantitative uniform normal-approximation upper bound and legal failure sequences proving necessity outside that regime. The formula/exponent is answer-open, not assumed. Strictly close the unresolved gap beyond the published sufficient d=o(n^(1/9)) condition, or show that condition sharp with a new legal obstruction. Defining the frontier by the original supremum or giving only a better unmatched sufficient exponent does not deliver the kernel. For W_ik=s_k 1[E_ik]/q_i (s_1=1,s_0=-1), let V=Cov_U(W), a known 2n×2n PSD matrix. VB=lambda_max(V)n^-2 sum_i(a_i²+b_i²); VBhat=lambda_max(V)n^-2 sum_i,k (Yobs_i)²1[E_ik]/q_i. Prove uniform VBhat/VB->1 in the normal regime and conservative coverage of T±z_(1-alpha/2)sqrt(VBhat) for each fixed alpha∈(0,1), with R fallback if VBhat=0. This estimates the conservative spectral variance bound, not the generally unidentifiable exact variance. Estimator algebra and class fixed; proof mechanism delegated. CONSUMER: DeclareDesign's published Research Design in the Social Sciences, section18.10/Declaration18.13, https://book.declaredesign.org/library/experimental-causal.html, implements the inquiry direct_ATE=mean(Y_1_0-Y_0_0) using the interference package for a lawn-sign/vote-margin design modeled after Green et al. (2016), The Effects of Lawn Signs on Vote Outcomes: Results from Four Randomized Field Experiments, Electoral Studies41:143–150. Its units are 238 Fairfax voting precincts; treatment is placement of candidate lawn signs, outcome is precinct vote margin, and the known undirected graph is geographic queen adjacency from poly2nb. The declared hop=1 model makes Y_i(e_i)=Y_1_0 and Y_i(0)=Y_0_0: signs in i with no neighboring signs versus no local signs. This is exactly this kernel's direct-effect inquiry, and the broader arbitrary-neighborhood class includes that exposure model. Changed practice: for future CGD replications of this SAME inquiry, replace the assignment/estimator by fixed CGD and use the derived degree rule to choose when its shorter Wald interval is justified rather than conservative Chebyshev calibration. The published declaration uses Bernoulli assignment and Aronow–Samii HT/Hajek, not CGD; no historical interval is retroactively validated, and the theorem gives an asymptotic benchmark rather than a finite-n certificate for the 238-precinct example.
PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A fresh presolve derived an exact forward Doob decomposition of the fixed r=2 estimator. Oriented-adjacency interpolation controls the sum of fourth increments by C B n lambda D²; a prefix-product coordinate-flip bound and Bernoulli variance tensorization control quadratic-variation variance by C B n lambda² D. A classical martingale normal-approximation theorem then suggests the sharp condition d_n=o(n^(2/3)). Repeated Perron-ordered stars give a Gaussian-plus-centered-Poisson boundary limit while preserving the original endpoint fourth moments and variance floor. A separate second-moment argument supports the stipulated spectral variance-bound estimator and conservative Wald coverage. Seven finite graph-family enumerations passed; these checks are not a universal proof. Direct substitutions in recent generic dependency-graph bounds did not supply the same frontier.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently audit the general coordinate-flip envelope and its operator-norm chain in draft equations (4.1)–(4.4), alongside the imported martingale theorem; the proposed exponent remains unverified.
EARLY KILL TEST: Prove or refute equation (4.2) for overlapping parent prefixes and arbitrary signed endpoints, especially shared-parent bipartite graphs. Stop this exponent claim if repair requires stronger graph or moment assumptions; retain the original answer-open problem for reassessment.
